Package glit.cli

Class GlitController

java.lang.Object
glit.cli.GlitController
public class GlitController extends Object

The central controller and command router for the Glit Version Control System CLI.

This class serves as the main entry point of the application. It captures command-line arguments, executes strict structural and state validations, expands file system wildcards, maps the inputs into executable Call contexts, and dispatches them to the underlying Repository service layer.

  • Method Details

    • expandWildcard

      public static List<Path> expandWildcard(String pattern) throws IOException

      Expands shell-like wildcard/glob patterns into a list of concrete file paths.

      This method normalizes shorthand patterns and performs file system traversal:

      • Transforms current directory shortcuts (. or ./) into a recursive wildcard (**).
      • Appends a recursive wildcard (/**) if the provided pattern points directly to an existing directory.
      • Walks the file tree from the current working directory, filtering out non-regular files and matching them against the glob engine.
      • Resolves all discovered paths relative to the repository root.
      Parameters:
      pattern - the glob/wildcard pattern string provided by the user (e.g., "*.txt", "src/")
      Returns:
      a List of Path objects matching the pattern, relative to the repository root
      Throws:
      IOException - if an error occurs during file system walking or path resolution

    • validateAndParseCommandLineArgs

      public static Call validateAndParseCommandLineArgs(String[] args) throws IOException

      Validates and parses raw command-line arguments into a structured execution token.

      The parsing process enforces several stateful and syntactic constraints:

      • Ensures a command function name is explicitly requested.
      • Blocks all operations (except init) if no valid .glit repository context exists.
      • Evaluates argument structures individually per command (init, add, commit, checkout, merge, cat-file, status, log, branch).
      • Handles flag abstractions (e.g., verifying -m for commits or -b for branch creations).
      • Performs automatic sanitation, such as replacing spaces with underscores in new branch names.

      If any validation checks fail, descriptive usage context is printed to standard output, and the routine aborts gracefully by returning null.

      Parameters:
      args - the raw array of command-line arguments passed from the application entry point
      Returns:
      a fully populated Call object ready for execution dispatch, or null if validation fails
      Throws:
      IOException - if an error occurs during wildcard resolution or repository configuration queries
